surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Kraken cruise past the Flames
paras: Jordan Eberle and Vince Dunn scored 32 seconds apart midway through the first to put the Kraken up 2-0. Frédérick Gaudreau made it 3-0 with 30 seconds left in the period. The third period was a wild one. Chandler Stephenson and Matty Beniers scored 51 seconds apart early in the period to stretch the lead to 5-0. Ryan Strome got the Flames on the board with three and a half minutes left, far too late to matter. Kaapo Kakko made it 6-1 for the Kraken 26 seconds later. Two players had three-point nights: Dunn with a goal and two assists, and Jared McCann with three assists.

The Kraken carried the play, outshooting the Flames 32-25, and got the result to match. Joey Daccord made 24 saves for the Kraken, and Dustin Wolf allowed six goals on 32 shots. The Kraken moved to 1-0-0, tied for first in the NHL in points percentage, while the Flames dropped to 0-1-0, still last in the NHL.

items.text: It was the first game of the season for both teams, and the Flames lost their home opener.
Frédérick Gaudreau extended his point streak against Calgary to six games.
